text:
maria: Heads-up — since the kernel 6.1.3 rollout to us-east-gpu nodes we've seen intermittent packet loss inside the overlay (small bursts, ~0.5-2%). Model-serving pods report gRPC stalls and retries. Noticed during normal east-west traffic between replicas.

sam: saw the same on canary pool, gRPC CANCELLED / deadline exceeded spikes. Any recent CNI changes?

jordan: no CNI changes. Rollout shows just the kernel upgrade and an updated mlx driver bundle this morning. deploy-bot: kernel-rollout/us-east-gpu completed @1987654210.

maria: tcpdump on pod veth shows occasional duplicate acks and some out-of-order. quick snippet: ```IP 10.2.3.45.49748 > 10.2.3.46.8080: Flags [P.], seq 123:267, ack 98, win 64240``` then nothing for 100-200ms.

lee: can we get ethtool -k and offload state from hosts? I suspect offload/GSO interaction with encapsulation.

sam: ethtool -k on host: tx-checksumming: on, sg: on, tso: on, gso: on, gro: on. geneve interface shows gso/tx offload as supported.

jordan: interestingly, NIC counters show TSO drops bumping on the affected nodes during bursts. That correlates with the gRPC spikes.

maria: I captured a pcap on the host and on the pod. Host pcap shows aggregated large segments, pod pcap shows fragmented small frames (after decap) and some appear dropped. Looks like offload/decap boundary mismatch.

lee: hypothesis: kernel 6.1.3 + mlx driver enabled a new offload path that hands off GSO to hardware for GENEVE decapsulation, but the CNI decap path isn't updated so some packets get mangled/dropped when decap occurs across NUMA or CPU shuffle.

sam: quick repro: disable tso/gso on host NIC, the errors vanish on the canary. Tried `ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off` and gRPC error rate dropped to baseline.

maria: thanks. Can we roll a targeted workaround? If we disable TSO/GSO cluster-wide that's costly but acceptable short term. Also could try `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` to avoid PMTUD blackholes; not sure it addresses decap offload mismatch though.

oncall: opening INC-1234 and marking priority P1 for us-east-gpu. Linking captures and host ethtool outputs: https://redwood.internal/ops/INC-1234 (internal).

jordan: longer-term options: 1) revert mlx driver to previous known-good, 2) file bug with upstream mlx/driver for offload/decap boundary, 3) update CNI to handle hardware-decapped segments correctly.

lee: plan: 1) disable TSO/GSO on the affected host pool (canary -> 10 hosts) and monitor for 1 hour, 2) keep kernel rollout paused for remaining us-east-gpu nodes, 3) open driver bug and schedule CNI test with patched driver.

maria: applied tso/gso off to canary, monitoring now. Initial 10 minutes look clean. If no regressions we'll extend to rest of pool and then coordinate with product for any perf hit.

sam: also adding a short-term probe in the runbook to detect TSO-drop spikes: `watch -n 5 ethtool -S eth0 | grep tso` and alert when >0.

jordan: noted. I'll start the driver bug template and include pcaps/ethtool stats.

infra-bot: INC-1234 updated: workaround applied to canary pool. ETA for wider mitigation 2h.

maria: thanks team. We'll keep this thread updated with rollout status and perf numbers.

lee: leaving a postmortem template in the ticket — include CPU pinning, NUMA, and decap offload tests for future kernel upgrades.

maria: final note — this felt subtle because packet counts looked normal on the underlay, only the decapped payloads were affected. Lesson: watch offload state changes when doing kernel/driver rollouts on overlay-heavy fleets. :warning:
